extracted.intended_audience: upper-level undergraduates and beginning graduate students studying algebraic topology (readers of a homology textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook exposition and proofs about singular and simplicial homology: barycentric subdivision, excision, equivalence of simplicial and singular homology, degree theory, and basic cellular homology facts for CW complexes. Contains statements, constructions, and conditions used to prove isomorphisms and compute homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lebesgue number for an open cover of a compact metric space
rubrics_metrics.description: A Lebesgue number for an open cover of a compact metric space is a number ε > 0 such that every set of diameter less than ε lies in some set of the cover; such a number exists by an elementary compactness argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to ensure that after sufficiently many barycentric subdivisions the diameter of simplices becomes small enough to lie inside elements of a given cover; provides the existence of m with Sm(σ) subordinate to the cover for each singular simplex σ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated barycentric subdivision chain homotopy
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain homotopy between the identity 11 and the iterate Sm is given by the operator Dm = sum_{0 ≤ i < m} T S^i, since ∂Dm + Dm∂ = 11 − Sm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit operator exhibits that iterated barycentric subdivision is chain homotopic to the identity; the calculation and telescoping sum show how the homotopy is constructed from the basic operator T and subdivision S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of chain map ρ subordinate to a cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Define D : C_n(X) → C_{n+1}(X) by Dσ = D_{m(σ)}σ for each singular n-simplex σ, where m(σ) is minimal so that S^{m(σ)}σ lies in the cover. Then define ρ = 11 − ∂D − D∂ so that ∂D + D∂ = 11 − ρ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a chain map ρ : C_n(X)→C^U_n(X) (chains subordinate to the cover) and a chain homotopy showing the inclusion of subordinate chains is a homotopy equivalence. The text checks ρ is a chain map and that ρ maps into the subordinate subcomplex by analyzing the terms Sm(σ)σ and differences Dm(σ)(σ_j) − Dm(σ_j)(σ_j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision theorem for decomposition X = A ∪ B (second version)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the cover U = {A, B} the inclusion C_n(A + B)/C_n(A) ↪ C_n(X)/C_n(A) induces an isomorphism on homology. The map C_n(B)/C_n(A ∩ B) → C_n(A + B)/C_n(A) induced by inclusion is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By factoring out chains in A the quotient maps inherit chain homotopy formulas ∂D + D∂ = 11 − ιρ and ρι = 11 so induce isomorphisms on homology; identification of bases of quotient groups shows H_n(B,A∩B) ≈ H_n(X,A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 2.22: quotient map for good pairs induces isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For good pairs (X, A), the quotient map q : (X, A) → (X/A, A/A) induces isomorphisms q_* : H_n(X, A) → H_n(X/A, A/A) ≈ H_n(X/A) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a neighborhood V of A in X that deformation retracts onto A to compare long exact sequences and apply excision; contractibility of CA and deformation retract of V/A onto A/A are used in related arguments. The hypothesis 'good pair' (existence of such a V) is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping cone identification of relative homology
rubrics_metrics.description: H_n(X, A) is isomorphic to H_n(X ∪ C A) for all n via the sequence of isomorphisms H_n(X ∪ C A) ≈ H_n(X ∪ C A, C A) ≈ H_n(X ∪ C A − {p}, C A − {p}) ≈ H_n(X, A), where C A is the cone on A and p its tip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses contractibility of C A, excision, and deformation retraction of C A − {p} onto A to identify relative homology with absolute homology of the mapping cone; provides a way to view relative homology as reduced absolute homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 2.24: excision property for CW subcomplexes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CW complex X is the union of subcomplexes A and B, then the inclusion (B, A ∩ B) ↪ (X, A) induces isomorphisms H_n(B, A ∩ B) → H_n(X, A) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows because CW pairs are 'good pairs', enabling the application of Proposition 2.22 and passage to quotients B/(A∩B) and X/A which are homeomorphic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 2.25: homology of wedge sum
rubrics_metrics.description: For a wedge sum ∨_α X_α, the inclusions i_α : X_α ↪ ∨_α X_α induce an isomorphism ⊕_α H_n(X_α) → H_n(∨_α X_α), provided the wedge is formed at basepoints x_α ∈ X_α and the pairs (X_α, x_α) are good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduced homology equals homology relative to a basepoint; apply Proposition 2.22 with (X,A) = (⊔_α X_α, ⊔_α {x_α}) to deduce the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.26: invariance of dimension via local homology
rubrics_metrics.description: If nonempty open sets U ⊂ R^m and V ⊂ R^n are homeomorphic, then m = n. This follows since H_k(U, U − {x}) ≅ H_k(R^m, R^m − {x}) ≅ Z for k = m and 0 otherwise, so the homeomorphism forces m = n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses excision, long exact sequence for the pair (R^m, R^m − {x}), and the deformation retraction of R^m − {x} onto S^{m−1} to compute local homology; demonstrates that local homology groups are topological invariants distinguishing dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and invariance of local homology groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Local homology groups of a space X at a point x ∈ X are defined to be H_n(X, X − {x}); for any open neighborhood U of x, excision gives H_n(X, X − {x}) ≅ H_n(U, U − {x}) assuming points are closed in X, so these groups depend only on the local topology near x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus homeomorphisms must induce isomorphisms on local homology groups at corresponding points; local homology can be used to detect non-homeomorphism of spaces near points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality of long exact sequences of pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: To say that the long exact sequence of a pair is natural means that for a map f : (X, A) → (Y, B) the induced diagram of homology groups is commutative. Commutativity involving boundary maps follows since f_♯ ∂ = ∂ f_♯ at the chain level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algebraic underpinning is that the long exact sequence associated to a short exact sequence of chain complexes is natural; this fact implies naturality for triples and reduced homology as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality of the long exact sequence from short exact sequences of chain complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: The long exact sequence of homology groups associated to a short exact sequence of chain complexes is natural: a commutative diagram of short exact sequences induces a commutative diagram of the associated long exact homology sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives the chain-level argument for commutativity of the boundary map squares and shows how this general algebraic fact yields naturality in many topological contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.27: equivalence of simplicial and singular homology
rubrics_metrics.description: For Δ-complex pairs (X, A) the canonical homomorphisms H_n^Δ(X, A) → H_n(X, A) are isomorphisms for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof first handles finite-dimensional X using the k-skeleton filtration and the five-lemma: compare relative groups H_n(X^k, X^{k−1}) which are zero except at n=k where both simplicial and singular groups are free with the same basis. Then extend to infinite-dimensional X using compactness of chain images and skeleton containment; handle general pairs via the five-lemma on long exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-Lemma (algebraic lemma used in proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a commutative diagram of abelian groups with exact rows, if α, β, δ, and ε are isomorphisms then γ is an isomorphism as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lemma is proved by standard diagram-chasing arguments: (a) surjectivity of γ follows if β and δ are surjective and ε injective; (b) injectivity of γ follows if β and δ are injective and α surjective. Used to lift isomorphisms from relative pieces to the middle term in long exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of homology for finite Δ-complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a Δ-complex with finitely many n-simplices then H_n(X) is finitely generated (since the simplicial chain group C_n^Δ(X) is finitely generated, so its subgroup of cycles and the quotient H_n(X) are finitely generated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Betti numbers are the number of Z summands in the decomposition of H_n(X), and torsion coefficients are the orders of finite cyclic summands; historically homology was viewed via Betti numbers and torsion coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of degree of a map S^n → S^n
rubrics_metrics.description: For f : S^n → S^n with n > 0, the induced map f_* : H_n(S^n) → H_n(S^n) is multiplication by some integer d depending only on f; this integer is called the degree of f, denoted deg f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree is a homotopy invariant and satisfies algebraic properties that allow computations and topological conclusions (see the listed properties (a)–(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of degree (a)–(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) deg 11 = 1. (b) deg f = 0 if f is not surjective. (c) If f ≃ g then deg f = deg g. (d) deg(f ∘ g) = deg f · deg g; so degree of homotopy equivalence is ±1. (e) A reflection has degree −1. (f) The antipodal map −11 has degree (−1)^{n+1}. (g) If f : S^n → S^n has no fixed points then deg f = (−1)^{n+1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each property is justified: (b) via factorization through a contractible complement, (c) via induced maps on homology, (d) functoriality, (e) and (f) via simplicial decompositions or composing reflections, (g) via homotopy to the antipodal map when no fixed points exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 2.29: constraints on groups acting freely on spheres
rubrics_metrics.description: Z_2 is the only nontrivial group that can act freely on S^n if n is even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: homeomorphisms have degree ±1, so an action determines a homomorphism d : G → {±1}; freeness forces nontrivial elements to have degree (−1)^{n+1}, so when n is even the degree homomorphism is injective and G ⊂ Z_2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 2.30: degree equals sum of local degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: If f : S^n → S^n and for some y ∈ S^n the preimage f^{-1}(y) consists of finitely many points x_1,...,x_m, then deg f = Σ_i deg(f, x_i), the sum of the local degrees at the preimages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses excision to decompose H_n(S^n, S^n − f^{-1}(y)) as a direct sum over neighborhoods of the preimages and tracks how inclusion/projection maps and f_* act on these summands to show the total degree is the sum of local degrees. Useful for computing degree by local analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing maps of prescribed degree (Example 2.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: To construct a map S^n → S^n of degree ±k take the quotient q : S^n → ∨^k S^n by collapsing the complement of k disjoint open balls to a point and then collapse the wedge ∨^k S^n → S^n identifying summands; precompose or compose with reflections to set local signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For almost all y the preimage consists of one point in each ball and each local degree is ±1; by choosing reflections one can realize any integer degree ±k. This provides an explicit construction method for maps with arbitrary degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 2.33: suspension preserves degree
rubrics_metrics.description: deg(S f) = deg f where S f : S^{n+1} → S^{n+1} is the suspension of f : S^n → S^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses cones and naturality of boundary maps in the long exact sequence of the pair (C S^n, S^n) to relate the induced homomorphisms and conclude degrees agree; geometrically S f has known behavior at the poles, matching local/global degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 2.34: cellular homology preliminaries for CW complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) H_k(X^n, X^{n−1}) is zero for k ≠ n and is free abelian for k = n with a basis in one-to-one correspondence with the n cells of X. (b) H_k(X^n) = 0 for k > n. (c) The map H_k(X^n) → H_k(X) induced by inclusion X^n ↪ X is an isomorphism for k < n and surjective for k = n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement (a) follows from X^n/X^{n−1} being a wedge of n-spheres (one per n-cell). The rest follow from the long exact sequence of the pair (X^n, X^{n−1}) and standard skeleton filtration arguments; proofs for infinite-dimensional X use compactness of chain images so chains lie in finite skeleta.
